llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, cogito_32b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0643 (median 0) and met the ≥75 % coverage threshold on just 60 % of cases, indicating that virtually all interactions produced negligible factual output. The failure analysis shows that 498 tasks (99.6 %) were diagnosed as erroneous, with the three most common error classes accounting for 71 % of failures: early termination (196 instances), no‑tool use (127) and task misunderstanding (89). Although the model attempted tool calls in 189 cases (38 % of tasks), the majority of errors were cognitive (309 tasks, 62 %), reflecting a systematic inability to translate retrieved data into a final answer rather than merely invoking the wrong API. A concrete remediation is to enforce a “must‑output” guard after the last successful tool call—e.g., a post‑processing step that checks for an empty final response and automatically triggers synthesis of all gathered facts before termination. What sets cogito_32b_output apart from other models is its pronounced early‑termination behavior: even when data are fetched correctly, the model frequently halts before any synthesis, leading to zero coverage despite successful tool usage.
